note: Participants shared across papers (codebook section 8). Each link gives one sample_id to the listed (cid, study_id) members, so that one record per sample, question, and comparison type enters a pooled estimate. When the sample_id starts with a member's paper key, that paper owns the sample, and its records win a primary tie; a reanalysis supplies the primary record only for a question the owner does not report (rule 4). A neutral id (shared__...) owns nothing: the usual rules and adjudication choose across the members. tools/make_sources.py applies the links.

links.basis: Meincke, Nave, and Terwiesch (2025) reanalyze the posted data of every Lee and Chung (2024) experiment; their S1 to S6 are Lee and Chung's Experiments 1, 2a, 2b, 3, 4, and 5 (study labels and counts match).

Screening forms of c041 and c246: the same 62-student within-person experiment with personalized versus standard generative-AI feedback, reported as a book chapter (c041) and a journal article (c246).
Screening forms of c089 and c471: the c089 ChatGPT arm and the c471 experimental arm have the same analyzed counts and procedures; treated as one sample so that no participant is counted twice.
Screening forms of c098 and c861: c861 reanalyzes an earlier human-AI brainstorming study, and identical participant quotations appear in both.
Screening forms of c031 and c201: both describe 51 third-year industrial design students at UPC in the same ideation experiment.
